title: Function interface telemetry-led validation and suggestive UX
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Define a lightweight authoring and runtime strategy that combines compact JSON invocation manifests with runtime telemetry to produce human-friendly validation errors and in-UI suggestive fixes. Scope includes: a compact DSL for required/optional params, provenance metadata for each parameter (who authored it, schema version), runtime validation modes (strict, permissive, suggest), telemetry hooks for validation failures, and a UX contract for presenting remediation suggestions to developers and solutions engineers. Out of scope: full schema evolution strategy and long-term storage of all validation events (handled by ENG-712345).
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: defined success metrics (reduce time-to-fix for invocation errors by 30%; reduce invalid call rate by 40%). See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/TOOL/Invocation+Telemetry+Validation

2026-02-25 - Spike complete: evaluated three approaches for capturing provenance (inline metadata, manifest-level ledger, external provenance service). Chose inline metadata with an optional provenance token to minimize round trips.
2026-03-02 - Design review (PM + DX): agreed on three validation modes. PM asked for an escape hatch 'suggest-only' mode for gradual rollouts.

2026-03-05 - Implementation note: validator implemented as a pluggable middleware in the runtime. Initial telemetry uses metrics: validation_failure_count, avg_time_to_fix_hint_clicks. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298
2026-03-10 - Security review requested (KMS interactions for provenance tokens). Security flagged token lifetime; recommended 24h default. Ticket linked: SEC-4482

2026-03-12 - QA feedback: suggestive messages are helpful but occasionally over-prescriptive; lowered suggestion aggressiveness for permissive mode. UX spec updated: https://docs.redwood.com/ux/invocation-suggestions-v1
acceptance_criteria: Authoring: authors can declare parameters with concise DSL (type, required, examples, hint) and optional provenance metadata
Runtime: validator exposes three modes (strict, permissive, suggest) configurable per-route and per-customer
Telemetry: validation failures emit consistent telemetry events with schema_version, route, customer_tier, and failure_reason
UX: Console surfaces the top 3 suggestion actions for each failure and provides a one-click 'apply suggestion' when safe
Backward compatibility: consumers with old manifests should fall back to permissive mode without runtime crashes
steps_taken: Created compact DSL prototype (YAML-like shorthand encoded in JSON). Example: {"param": {"t":"str", "r":true, "ex":"foo"}}
Implemented runtime middleware that normalizes incoming manifest to canonical schema and emits validation telemetry
Built suggest engine that maps common failures to tokenized corrective hints (type coercion, missing required, enum mismatch)
Added feature flag to enable 'suggest' mode per-route; default off for enterprise customers until 2026-04
decision: Adopt inline compact manifest with optional provenance token. Use three runtime validation modes to balance safety and gradual rollout. Provide suggestive UX powered by telemetry-driven frequent-failure mappings. This minimizes latency impact while enabling observable remediation flows.
next_steps: Merge runtime PR and enable feature-flagged rollout for internal teams (Q1 post-merge)
Coordinate with Console team to implement top-3 suggestion surface and 'apply suggestion' action
Create migration notes for customers with legacy manifests and enable permissive fallback by default
Follow up with Security for token lifetime policy and update SEC-4482
